study_families.design: Single-arm, prospective, within-person pre-post observational cohort (no non-exercise comparator arm); post-hoc stratified by incident lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) during 2-week follow-up.
study_families.training_load: Cohort-level: median ~10 y running experience, ~6.5 h/week training before the marathon (Table 1); no formal pre-marathon training-load protocol reported.
study_families.cointerventions: NR (no experimental co-intervention; authors note feeding/hydration status was not controlled and raise it as a limitation, p.8).
study_families.study_notes: Ethics approval: Comite Etic de Investigacio Clinica de la Fundacio de Gestio Sanitaria del Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau, project IIBSP-SUMMIT-2016-02 (p.2); this is an ethics-approval number, not a trial registry ID.

reports.title: Salivary immunity and lower respiratory tract infections in non-elite marathon runners
reports.authors: Canto E; Roca E; Perea L; Rodrigo-Troyano A; Suarez-Cuartin G; Giner J; Feliu A; Soria JM; Nescolarde L; Vidal S; Sibila O
reports.version_label: Version of record, PLOS ONE 13(11): e0206059, published 21 Nov 2018
reports.inclusion_reason: Identifiable single bout (2016 Barcelona Marathon, 42.195 km) with a pre-race baseline (1 day before) and a post-cessation sample (2 days after, within the 0-72h organising window) in healthy adults (mean age ~39-40 y); direct immune-linked measurements (salivary sIgA/AMPs/chemokines ELISA panel; blood leukocyte differential, CRP) satisfy immune_link; prospectively tracked LRTI over 2 weeks post-race.
reports.reviewer_notes: Provisional INCLUDE_A (Core A): single identifiable bout, baseline + within-window post sample, adult cohort, direct immune measurements plus a self-reported clinical (LRTI) outcome. See unresolved_questions for age-reporting inconsistency and per-marker denominator variability.
reports.author_stated_use: NR (authors do not state an explicit intended clinical/monitoring 'use' of the markers beyond describing their relationship with LRTI risk; Discussion frames markers as candidates for understanding 'the development of LRTI after races', p.8-9, not as a named application such as return-to-training or diagnosis).
author_window_interpretation_locator: p.2 Introduction: 'Within two weeks of completing such strenuous exercise, the risk of infection increased 100% to 500%'; p.8 Discussion: 'athletic performance is both a stress factor ... that may help to prevent disease' / 'immunological status may be important for the development of a LRTI'; the term 'open window' itself does not appear in the text.

cohorts.baseline_health: Healthy non-elite marathon runners; excluded if reported respiratory symptoms in the 2 weeks before the race; all baseline labs (glucose, electrolytes, CBC, CRP) in normal range (Table 1).
cohorts.age_sex: 28 male, 19 female; All runners age 39.0+-7.1 y (Table 1, mean+-SD); BMI higher in males than females (23.6+-2.1 vs 20.7+-1.4, p=0.01).
cohorts.training_status: Non-elite/recreational marathon runners; median years training ~10 (9.7+-9.3), ~6.5 h/week (6.5+-3.7) (Table 1).
cohorts.sport: Marathon running (42.195 km road race, 2016 Barcelona Marathon)
cohorts.cohort_notes: Single cohort, no sub-strata by recruitment source; post-hoc split into No-LRTI (n=39, 21M/18F) vs LRTI (n=8, 7M/1F) for several comparisons (Table 1).
cohorts.age_range: UNCLEAR - internally inconsistent: Results text states 'Median age was 30 years old' (p.4) but Table 1 reports mean age 39.0+-7.1 y for all runners (p.4); no min-max range given either way.

report_cohort_links.link_notes: Single report, single cohort, single bout; LRTI vs no-LRTI is an outcome-based subgroup split of the same cohort, not a separate recruited cohort.

ai_assistance.task_prompt_version: 10-report charting pilot, reviewer B AI stand-in instructions (2026-10-05)

extraction_provenance.open_data: No external dataset/accession beyond the PLOS S1 File raw-data spreadsheet (R59_supp_pone.0206059.s001.xlsx), which is openly accessible under the article's CC BY licence; no GEO/SRA-type accession applicable.
extraction_provenance.integrity_status: No correction/retraction notice visible on the PDF/landing information reviewed 2026-10-05; not independently cross-checked against PubMed/Crossref update records beyond the PDF itself.
extraction_provenance.provenance_notes: AI-assisted charting pilot extraction per PILOT_README.md Section 5-7; AI did not make eligibility or value-judgment decisions beyond applying the controlled vocabularies as instructed. See eligibility_opinion and unresolved_questions in the companion JSON for judgment calls flagged for human review.

eligibility_opinion.rationale: Identifiable single bout (2016 Barcelona Marathon, 42.195 km) with a pre-race baseline sample (1 day before, p.3) and a post-cessation sample at ~48 h (2 days after the race, within the 0-72h organising window, p.3) in a healthy adult cohort (p.2); direct immune-linked measurements (salivary sIgA/AMPs/chemokine ELISA panel, blood leukocyte differential, p.3-4) satisfy the immune-link rule and a self-reported clinical outcome (LRTI, p.2-3) is tracked for 2 weeks post-race.

unresolved_questions: cohorts.age_range: Results text states 'Median age was 30 years old' (p.4) but Table 1 reports mean age 39.0+-7.1 y for all runners (p.4); these cannot both be correct and the source of the discrepancy (typo vs wrong summary statistic) cannot be resolved from the PDF alone.

sample_sets.missing_data: per-marker analysable n within the nominal 47-runner cohort varies widely (e.g. IgA n=43-44, lysozyme n=22+8=30, chemokines n=17+6=23, per the S1 File raw-data columns) with no stated reason in the main text; unclear whether the manual wants separate sample_sets rows per marker when denominators differ this much, or whether a single sample_set with a missing_data note (as done here) is sufficient.

measurements.marker_family: the controlled vocabulary has no explicit category for salivary antimicrobial proteins (lactoferrin, lysozyme); they were filed under 'other', which may not be what a future validation-readiness map intends - recommend the team consider a dedicated marker_family value or explicit mapping rule.

precision_validation granularity: the manual states domains are recorded 'per report/cohort/measurement', which could mean per single analyte (6+ rows x 7 domains for this report alone) rather than per marker-group as done here (4 groups x 7 = 28 rows); grouping closely related analytes (e.g. the three chemokines) was a pragmatic pilot choice that should be confirmed with A/D.

clinical_endpoint vocabulary: LRTI here is ascertained by a formal symptom-based case definition (ERS/ESCMID criteria plus fever/duration rules, p.2) applied to self-reported symptoms, with no clinician visit described; it is unclear whether this should be coded self_reported_symptoms (used here) or clinician_defined_syndrome given the formal criteria.

measurements.result_direction for correlation rows (M-R59-012/013/014): the controlled vocabulary (increase/decrease/no_detected_difference/mixed_or_inconsistent) is designed for group/time comparisons, not correlation coefficients; 'mixed_or_inconsistent' was used as the closest fit but this may need a dedicated value for association/correlation results.

reports.author_stated_use and author_window_interpretation: the paper never uses the phrase 'open window' and never states an explicit marker 'use'; both fields required an interpretive judgment call (classified as immunosuppression_or_susceptibility_without_term / NR) that should be checked against Reviewer C's independent reading.
